High-level proposed cadence (we can edit):
- Week 0: Trial cluster (2x A100-equivalent) smoke tests (redwood-managed)
- Week 2: Extended eval with performance targets (50 qps sustained for 4 hrs)
- Week 4: Canary (staging traffic) with 25% traffic shift
- Week 6: Full reservation + go-live (reserve N GPUs per MAP)

I've cc'd Karthik and Neha from our capacity planning team for sizing/lead-time guidance and Ben for procurement coordination.

Attachments: MAP_draft_ACME_v1.pdf (draft MAP), GPU_Sizing_Scenarios_ACME.xlsx (scenarios), Acceptance_Criteria_Guide.md (checklist)

Subject: Re: Evaluation -> Procurement checklist: GPU pool sizing & reservation scenarios

Hi all — quick sizing note based on your projected throughput and the eval telemetry: 

Summary recommendation (see attached workbook for details):
- Conservative initial reservation (fastest time-to-stable): 24 x A100-equivalent GPUs across 3 nodes (8 GPUs/node) — supports sustained 250 qps inference profiles with 90th pct latency < 200ms with our batching and KV cache.
- Cost-optimized ramp (min upfront cost): Start with 8 x A100-equivalent for canary (2 nodes) + burst pool (auto-burst 16 GPUs) for peak windows; convert to reserved 16 GPUs after 30 days of stable telemetry.
- Eval-only small cluster: 2 x A100-equivalent (trial cluster) for functional/perf validation.

Lead-time considerations: procurement for reserved capacity typically needs 6–9 weeks from PO to guaranteed tranche availability for dedicated pools depending on region and GPU SKU. If Acme requires specific physical isolation or on-prem racks, add 10–14 weeks for coordination and delivery.

Acceptance criteria for eval -> canary -> reserve (draft):
- Eval: model correctness + perf smoke (50 qps sustained for 4 hrs)
- Canary: 25% traffic with <1% error rate and latency SLOs met for 7 consecutive days
- Reserve: 99th pct latency within agreed threshold and cost forecast approved

I'll add these to the MAP draft and can produce a variant that ties milestones to dates once we have the PO window.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. Sara, based on the PO timing you shared (signed terms by 1/05, PO by 1/20) here's a proposed mutually agreed timeline that maps to procurement cutoffs. Please review and flag conflicts: 

Proposed MAP milestones (dates tentative):
- 12/08 - 12/22: Eval (trial cluster) — functional & perf smoke (2 x A100-equiv)
- 12/23 - 01/05: Extended eval + telemetry window (expand to 8 GPUs if more parallelism needed)
- 01/06 - 01/19: Canary staging (staging traffic, 25% shift)
- 01/20: PO submitted by Acme (target) — Redwood to confirm tranche reservation within 48 hrs
- 01/21 - 02/28: Reserved capacity provisioning (conservative: 24 GPUs) — go-live once provisioning validated

Key decisions we need from Acme to lock dates:
1) Preferred reservation scenario: conservative (24 GPUs) or cost-optimized ramp (start small + burst)?
2) Any legal/contractual SLA deviations required (we default to Redwood Dedicated SLA 99.9% — Laura, pls advise if exceptions requested)?
3) Data residency confirmation (us-east-1 for prod).

If procurement can commit to the 1/20 PO target we can guarantee hold on the tranche that supports the conservative scenario. If not, we can offer a temporary burst pool option but it carries a risk of delayed capacity guarantees.

I'm proposing a short 30-minute call Thursday to finalize. When are you available?

—Marissa

Marissa — procurement here. A few notes from our side: 

- PO window: we can target 01/20 but need commercial terms signed no later than 01/05 (legal sign-off). Please confirm the commercial term doc (we prefer a short form SOW + PO).
- SLA: 99.9% is acceptable. We will list a remedy matrix in commercial terms (credits).
- Data residency: confirmed, prod must be us-east-1. Will require an SOC2 attestation and access to audit logs during canary.
- Payment terms: Net 30 preferred. Any contract language that mentions reserved capacity billing in advance needs to be explicit (we cannot prepay more than 90 days without treasury approval).

We will send a PO template and a redline to the commercial term doc by 12/17. Please confirm Redwood can provide SOC2 evidence and a 30-day trial invoice/credit for the eval cluster.

—Procurement

- Reservation scenario: conservative initial reservation — 24 x A100-equivalent GPUs (3x nodes). We will provision a 2-GPU trial cluster immediately for eval.
- PO timeline: commercial terms sign-off by 01/05, PO issued by 01/20. Redwood to place tranche hold within 48 hrs of PO.
- Data residency & compliance: production to run in us-east-1. Redwood to provide SOC2 report and audit log access during canary.
- Billing: reserved capacity billed monthly; Redwood accepts Net 30. No prepayment >90 days required.

Action items: 
- Acme procurement: return redlined commercial terms by 12/17 and confirm PO approver list.
- Acme cloudops: provide final traffic profile for canary by 12/22 (expected QPS and payload sizes).
- Redwood (Karthik/Neha): lock tranche and share provisioning ETA once PO received; prepare an operations runbook for canary + rollback.
- Marissa/Ben/Laura: prepare signature package (DocuSign) once redlines are resolved.
